title: Competitive Signal Ontology + Vendor Switch-Cost Heatmap
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a canonical ontology for competitive signals (pricing, API surface changes, behavioral regressions, latency/p95 shifts, quantization availability) and build a vendor switch-cost heatmap that maps observable signals to likely procurement friction and commercial impact. The goal is to enable timely product + GTM responses: automated alerts for high-risk vendor events, prioritized scouting for fallback models, and economic impact estimates. This ticket covers taxonomy design, ingestion requirements, minimal dashboard mock, and actionable procurement scoring heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Ontology doc published with categories, attributes, and signal priority (confluence link provided)
Ingestion schema defined and handed to Eng (Kafka topic + sample payloads)
Prototype heatmap dashboard mock accessible in Looker/Console with sample data
Scoring rubric that converts signal bundles into switch-cost buckets (low/medium/high) with confidence bands
decisions: Use hybrid approach: combine automated telemetry (synthetic workload probes + public pricing API scraping) and curated field reports from Sales/SEs
Initial retention window for raw signals set to 90 days for analysis, 365 days for aggregated metrics
Score formula will weigh immediate availability signals (outages, API contract changes) higher than slow-drip signals (minor latency regressions) for procurement triggers
